newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Arms found at Kuwait oil export terminal-official.
newsitem.headline: Arms found at Kuwait oil export terminal-official.

text.p: Kuwait said on Wednesday it had found weapons and ammunition hidden at its crude oil and refined products export terminal of Mina al-Ahmadi.
"Weapons have been found...and an investigation is underway to find out why they were stored," the head of the interior ministry's public relations department, Colonel Adel al-Ibrahim, told Reuters.

Ibrahim, who said the ministry might issue a detailed statement at a later stage, was commenting on a report in al-Rai al-Aam newspaper which said that the arms, including hand grenades and rocket-propelled grenades, were not related to the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
It said they were recently placed there "for later use".

Following the 1991 Gulf War, all strategic installations in the tiny Gulf Arab state were swept for weapons and land mines left behind by fleeing Iraqi troops. Ahmadi was among sites which were carefully searched.

The daily quoted "informed sources" as saying in the front- page report that the Interior Ministry found the arms hidden in a room at Ahmadi where state refiner Kuwait National Petroleum Company has a 440,000 barrel per day refinery.

"The sources said the arms were very carefully stored. The method of storing does not indicate that the weapons were left behind after the (1990) Iraqi invasion (of Kuwait), but it indicates that they were recently placed at the port...and stored for later use," the newspaper added.
Ahmadi is a major exporter of middle distillates such as gas oil (diesel) and kerosene to Asia and the Indian subcontinent.
Kuwait, a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), has a two million bpd quota and a local refining capacity of about 850,000 bpd.
